native_result.query: Between which two races is the factor of BA degree completion -0.9568 when compared to the other?
native_result.HypoA: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.
native_result.HypoB: The factor −0.9568 for BA degree completion — interpreted, with White as the reference, as the logistic-regression log-odds coefficient on a race indicator — uniquely identifies the comparison **Hispanic vs. White**. Across the two sanctioned specifications the Hispanic-vs-White coefficient is consistently closer to −0.9568 than the Black-vs-White coefficient: two-group restricted standard-MLE logit β̂_Hispanic = −0.9241 vs β̂_Black = −1.0057; two-group restricted Firth (Jeffreys-prior) penalized logistic β̂_Hispanic = −0.9479 vs β̂_Black = −1.0209. The Hispanic-vs-White Firth estimate is just 0.009 from the target; −0.9568 was not reproduced to machine precision by any tested specification, but the pair pinning is robust. Final natural-language hypothesis: Hispanic respondents have substantially lower log-odds of completing a BA degree than White respondents (raw completion 1.44 % vs 3.54 %; adjusted OR ≈ 0.40).

The Hispanic-vs-White Firth estimate is approximately 0.009 from the target. No tested specification reproduces −0.9568 to machine precision, but the comparison identification is robust. Hispanic respondents have lower BA completion log-odds than White respondents.
